review: That first cup never seemed to be the last. The Osmania biscuit was part of the plan; staying for hours wasn’t.
story: We’d go in for a cup of chai, thinking we’d leave soon. Since it was a nice place to sit, we’d end up staying for hours, talking and pulling each other’s leg.
imageAlt: Niloufer Irani chai cup with Osmania biscuits

review: Sweeter than Niloufer’s, and its flavour lingers long after the cup is empty. I like this one even more.
story: I like Niloufer’s chai, but I like this one even more. It’s sweeter, and I can still taste it long after the cup is finished.

review: Quick, hot, and dependable. When I’m hungry and want a proper plate of chicken biryani without overthinking it, Mehfil is the easy call.
Same chicken-and-rice comfort, but with a much bigger kick and a flavour of its own. I go for it when regular dum biryani feels too mild.
Chaat from the Mathrusree Nagar bandi: crunchy, tangy, spicy, and hard to stop picking at. One of my Hyderabad favourites.
The fried rice I keep going back to—hot, savoury, and properly filling. Sometimes that’s all I need from dinner.
Cool mint with little chocolate chips in every spoonful. Exactly the scoop I want when I’m in the mood for something cold and sweet.
imageAlt: A scoop of ice cream in a cone

review: A few little chitti bondas, then prawn upma when a snack clearly isn’t enough. Two different cravings, sorted in one stop.
imageAlt: Golden Indian snacks served with chutney

review: Fragrant, spiced rice with prawns tucked through the plate. Prawn pulao is the order I remember from One Drive In.
imageAlt: A simple rice dish with accompaniments

review: Golden-edged, soft-centred ponganalu cooked with ghee and served with chutney. A little South Indian tiffin plate I’m glad I tried.
imageAlt: South Indian breakfast served on a banana leaf

review: Brownie, vanilla ice cream, chocolate fudge, and crunchy nuts all piled into one bowl. Definitely not a subtle chocolate dessert.
